deep.reconstruction:
The page treats one problem: the diagonal rational (Padé) approximation of a power series and its link to continued fractions.

(1) Setup. f(x)=sum_{nu>=0} a_nu x^nu. Riemann seeks P(x)/Q(x) with P=b_0+...+b_m x^m and Q=c_0+...+c_m x^m such that P/Q agrees with f up to and including x^{2m}. Multiplying out (Q f = P + O(x^{2m+1})) gives two sets of conditions.
- Homogeneous equations (coefficients of x^{m+1},...,x^{2m}): c_0 a_{m+k} + c_1 a_{m+k-1} + ... + c_m a_k = 0 for k=1..m. The page lists them from k=m (c_0 a_{2m}+...+c_m a_m=0) down to k=1 (c_0 a_{m+1}+c_1 a_m+...+c_m a_1=0).
- Numerator coefficients: b_k = sum_{j<=k} c_j a_{k-j}. The page lists b_m = c_0 a_m+...+c_m a_0, b_{m-1}, ..., b_1 = c_0 a_1 + c_1 a_0, b_0 = c_0 a_0.

(2) Determinant solution (Cramer's rule). Re-index the m x (m+1) system with columns j'=m-j, so the entries become a_{k+j'}. Then c_nu is, up to sign, the m x m minor obtained by deleting one column.
- c_0 = sum ± a_{1+0+0} a_{1+1+1} ... a_{1+(m-1)+(m-1)} = det(a_{1+i+j})_{i,j=0..m-1}, a Hankel determinant in a_1..a_{2m-1}.
- c_1: the last diagonal entry becomes a_{1+(m-1)+m}.
- c_nu: in general, the column of index m-nu is deleted.
These indices are consistent with the system.

(3) Integral representation of the determinants. Implicitly a_n = (1/2πi)∮ f(t) t^{-n-1} dt (my filling). Insert this row by row into the determinant; each row then carries its own variable t_k. The remaining determinant in the powers of t_k is a Vandermonde determinant. The result is
c_0 = const·∮...∮ prod_{k=1}^m f(t_k) dt_k / t_k^{m+k} · prod_{a<b}(t_a - t_b).
The exponents are m+1, m+2, ..., 2m. The page shows t_1^{m+1}, t_2^{m+1} (probably meant m+2), and a corrected last exponent that is hard to read. Symmetrizing gives the Heine form (1/m!)∮ prod f(t_k) t_k^{-2m} dt_k prod_{a<b}(t_a-t_b)^2; this symmetrized form is not on the page.

(4) Cauchy kernel. The marginal notes ds/(s-x) and x^n/s^{n+1} refer to 1/(s-x) = sum x^n/s^{n+1}, and to its tail x^N/(s^N(s-x)).

(5) Remainder formula (my derivation of what the line expresses).
- E(x) = Q(x)f(x) - P(x) = sum_{n>=2m+1} (sum_j c_j a_{n-j}) x^n.
- Each coefficient is (1/2πi)∮ f(s)Q(s)s^{-n-1}ds, so E(x) = x^{2m+1}(1/2πi)∮ f(s)Q(s) ds/(s^{2m+1}(s-x)).
- Q(s) is the (m+1)x(m+1) determinant: rows (a_{m+k-j})_{j=0..m} for k=1..m, plus the row (s^j).
- Inserting the integrals for the a's gives Q(s) = const·∮ prod_k f(t_k) dt_k / t_k^{m+k+1} · prod_{a<b}(t_a-t_b) · prod_a (s-t_a).
- Riemann's line c∫ f(s) ds/(s-x) f(t_1)dt_1/t_1^{m+2} f(t_2)dt_2/t_2^{m+3} ... f(t_m)dt_m/t_m^{2m+1} Π(t_a-t_b) Π(s-t_a) matches this exactly. The exponents m+2..2m+1 are right; the factor (x/s)^{2m+1} is not written (it appears only via the x^n/s^{n+1} note).
This is the multiple-integral (Heine-type) representation of the Padé denominator and of the error.

(6) Iterated integrals and Taylor remainder.
- f(x) = f(0) + ∫_0^{x_1} f'(0) + ... is written as iterated integrals over x_1>x_2>...>x_m>0, ending in f^{(m)}.
- Integral remainders: ∫_0^x f'(s)ds = x f'(0) - ∫_0^x f''(s)(s-x)ds (page has +), and x f'(0) + f''(0)x^2/2 + ∫_0^x f'''(s)(s-x)^2/2 ds (correct).

(7) Continued fraction. Riemann starts f(x) = f(0) + x f'(0)/(1+...). Each tail is written as an exact quotient of integral remainders, e.g. -∫f''(s)(s/x-1)ds / (x f'(0) + ∫f''(s)(s/x-1)ds), and then 1/(1 + ∫f'''(s)(s-x)^2/2 / (f''(0)x^2/2)). The leading partial numerators are x f'(0) and -(x f''(0)/2)/f'(0). He also tries the form f(0)/(1 - (f'(0)/f(0))x/(1+...)). This is the corresponding (C-) continued fraction, whose convergents are the staircase Padé approximants, with exact integral remainders. The fragment breaks off.
errors: The line ∫_0^x f'(s)ds = x f'(0) + ∫_0^x f''(s)(s-x)ds has a sign slip; it should be -∫ f''(s)(s-x)ds = +∫ f''(s)(x-s)ds. Later quotients use -∫f''(s)(s/x-1)ds, so it is effectively corrected.
In the c_0 integral the exponents should be t_k^{m+k} (m+1,...,2m). The page shows t_2^{m+1} and a struck/unclear last exponent, so the exponents are at least partly wrong or unclear.

The remainder integral omits the factor x^{2m+1}/s^{2m+1} (only ds/(s-x) is written), and the constant c is unspecified. Taken literally, the formula is a representation of Q-related quantities rather than the exact error E(x).
The c_nu formula is left incomplete (a stray 'a'), and the signs ± of the minors are not fixed.

results.what: Linear system for the [m/m] rational approximant of a power series (denominator from the Hankel system, numerator by convolution)
results.usually_credited_to: Jacobi 1846, Frobenius 1881, Padé 1892 (Cauchy 1821 for rational interpolation)

results.what: Denominator coefficients as Hankel-type minors of the moment array
results.modern_name: Jacobi's determinant formula for Padé denominators

results.what: Hankel determinant and Padé denominator as m-fold contour integrals with a Vandermonde factor, prod f(t_k)t_k^{-(m+k+1)} prod(t_a-t_b) prod(s-t_a), giving an integral formula for the error
results.modern_name: Heine's multiple-integral representation of orthogonal polynomials / Hankel determinants (Andreief–Heine identity), applied to Padé remainders
results.usually_credited_to: Heine (Handbuch der Kugelfunctionen, 1878-81 ed.), Andreief 1883; Padé error integrals later (Padé, Pólya–Szegő, Nuttall)

results.what: Taylor expansion via iterated integrals and integral remainder
Corresponding continued fraction f(0)+x f'(0)/(1 - x f''(0)/(2f'(0))/(1+...)) with exact integral tails
results.modern_name: C-fraction / corresponding continued fraction (Padé table staircase)

deep.surprise_reason: Padé equations, Jacobi determinants and the Taylor remainder are routine for the period. Riemann's interest in continued fractions and rational approximation is known from his 1863 hypergeometric continued-fraction fragment. The non-routine element is the correct multiple-integral (Vandermonde-weighted) representation of the Padé denominator and error. This is essentially Heine's formula, usually dated to Heine (1878) and Andreief (1883). If the folio is from the 1850s, it would be a notable unpublished anticipation. The page is fragmentary, though, and the symmetrized Heine form does not appear explicitly.

checkable.asserts: m=1 case: c0=a1 (Riemann's det a_{1+0+0}), c1=-a2, b0=c0 a0, b1=c0 a1+c1 a0 give agreement through x^2

transcription_corrections: 'c_1 = c_0 a_1 + c_1 a_0' should read 'b_1 = c_0 a_1 + c_1 a_0'.
The note 't^n/s^n ∂s/(s-x)' is likely 'x^n/s^n · ds/(s-x)' (Cauchy-kernel tail).
In the c_0 integral, the exponent of t_2 looks like m+1 but should be m+2 (pattern m+k). The last exponent is struck and replaced; the '2m-1' reading is uncertain.
In the remainder integral the exponents read m+2, m+3, ..., 2m+1, and the products are Π(t_a - t_b) Π(s - t_a).
The partial numerator '-x^2/2 f''0 / f'0' is likely '-x/2 f''(0)/f'(0)' (or x^2 if paired with x f'(0) as numerator).
